ecology_people.note: Per-billion costs of the lunar design and Earth practice, rain-fed land and diets (people_and_land.md).

places.note: Main's corrected Earthlight per place (each place's own sky); this branch's copy predates it.

evidence: Grid sums on the 28% atlas, the drainage lakes and rivers and the design climatology (A28_dim5_moon), twilight from the solved clear sky, and closed-form arithmetic on committed products and two bound inputs. The settings are possibilities drawn from the project's designs; their densities, mixes and shares are stated assumptions. No climate, flow, structural, ecological or social model runs, and no placement of people is chosen.
reading_rule: People in billions unless named; areas km2; water km3 a year; energy and heat TW (per billion residents, TW equals kW a person); mass Gt (1e12 kg); shares are fractions and _percent values percentage points. Pairs are [low, high]. Energy keys are the provisioning band (2.0, 3.68 and 5.99 kW of primary energy a person); heat on the Moon takes the band with industry in orbit and thermal plants. Kept shares are the author's 30% and half of the land. Light entries of null after sunset last the whole night. Bound inputs are named under producer.bound_inputs.

mixes.spread: People in proportion to each setting's home land.
mixes.waterfront: Four times as dense on the shores and wet margins.
mixes.rain_belt: Four times as dense where the rain grows the food: farms, forest edges and wet margins.
mixes.cool_ground: Four times as dense on the cooler ground both climate models find comfortable: highlands and the middle and high latitudes.

aerial_mixes.roaming: Every sky town roams, powered 1-10% of the time at 5 m/s through the air.
aerial_mixes.half_moored: Half roam; half are moored by tethers over fixed places.
aerial_mixes.streamlined: Every sky town is a streamlined hull holding its place against the wind.

assumptions.shared_homes: Farming country and canopy towns share the rain-belt interior evenly; highland towns and districts held up by terrain share the highlands evenly.
assumptions.fixed_people: The summit metropolis holds its planned 100 million in every mix; the undersea communities their domes; the high platforms carry crews only.
assumptions.water_density: 1 kg per litre of fresh water
assumptions.food: Crops grow on the rain alone in the bands where most land is wet, wettest land first; the crops that land cannot hold are irrigated at the crop model's yield with water lifted from the seas to the mean land height.
assumptions.lit_sky: Every lunar resident, aloft as on the ground, lights ecology's lunar-design lit sky a person.
assumptions.rain_catchment: Sky towns catch the ground's rain rate on their projected area; the climatology holds no rain by height.

winds.rule: Holding a time of day takes an airspeed of |u + v_sun| eastward and |v| northward against the Sun-frame mean wind at the best hour, with the spread of the 3-day means (10th to 90th percentile over 2.563 standard deviations) added in quadrature; the streamlined hull pays the cube of that airspeed.

summit_metropolis.name: The summit metropolis and its port
summit_metropolis.character: A beautiful, sustainable metropolis of about 100 million round the Moon's largest sky port on the far side's summit, 11.6 km above the sea, in the coolest open air of any city. Districts gather round crater lakes; sky boats serve as cars and gliders fly throughout, and a backbone of metro, rail and sky ferries carries it. The port's rings and disks hold parks to 15 km and the Moon's only winter.
summit_metropolis.third_dimension: The port tower to 35.6 km, with parks for everyone to 3 km above the summit; sky boats to 1.5 km, ferries to 2.5 km, gliders on thermals to about 10 km by day; a glider launched from ring 0 reaches anywhere in the city.

coastal_and_lake_towns.name: Coastal and lake towns
coastal_and_lake_towns.character: Harbour towns on the seas and great lakes: the near-side sea's long coasts, the far side's South Pole-Aitken sea, islands such as Caucasus and Jura, and the shores of the highland lakes such as Korolev and Hertzsprung. The monthly tide lays out flats for days, and the seas are gentle and fresh for their first thousands of years.
coastal_and_lake_towns.third_dimension: Sky ferries and harbours for regional ships; gliders along the shore; from a 100 m headland the sea is in view for 18.6 km.

wetland_edge_towns.name: Wetland-edge towns
wetland_edge_towns.character: Towns at the wet margins: the shores of the many small crater lakes and the floodplains of the large rivers, among reed belts and wetland mosaics, with water travel and boardwalk streets.
wetland_edge_towns.third_dimension: Boardwalks and raised districts over the wet ground; personal wings over the reed beds.

canopy_towns.name: Canopy-connected towns at forest edges
canopy_towns.character: Towns at the edges of forests 100-500 m tall, whose routes rise through the forest's layers on their own supports beside the trees, with gliders launched from the crowns and the dim lower forest kept for quiet trails.
canopy_towns.third_dimension: Walkways and stations through the canopy layers; a micro glider launched from a 300 m crown glides 4.5 km at 15 to 1.

farming_country.name: Rain-belt farming country
farming_country.character: Villages and market towns among the farms of the rain belt: plains of storage organs and orchards of day fruit set at sunrise and ripe at sunset, so harvest, travel and markets gather at dusk.
farming_country.third_dimension: Cargo drones and sky vans between farm and market; harvest freighters to the cities.

highland_towns.name: Highland and ridge towns
highland_towns.character: Towns on ground 4 km and more above the sea, in cooler air: terraces on crater walls, ridges in the fog-garden country of the middle latitudes, and the rainy upland rise round the summit.
highland_towns.third_dimension: Terraces down crater walls kilometres high; glider launches from the rims.

elevated_districts.name: Districts held up by towers or terrain
elevated_districts.character: Districts carried along crater walls and ridges or held up on towers, where the same steel reaches two and a half to three times as high as on Earth and sky boats reach the upper floors.
elevated_districts.third_dimension: Floors high above open ground; parks on the roofs; a canopy lowers a person at 4 m/s from any rim.

nearside_towns.name: Nearside towns under the fixed Earth
nearside_towns.character: Inland towns of the comfortable middle latitudes on the near side. The Earth stands in the same place in the sky all month, near full at midnight, and where it stands high it keeps the night near the light at which Earth's civil twilight ends.
nearside_towns.third_dimension: Sky boats and ferries between towns; the Earth in view from every height.

limb_towns.name: Limb towns where the Earth rises and sets
limb_towns.character: Towns along the limb, where the libration lifts the Earth above the horizon and lowers it again once a month.
limb_towns.third_dimension: Height lifts the Earth into view: from 1 km up the horizon dips by 1.9 degrees.

far_side_places.name: The far side's twilit-night places
far_side_places.character: The far side's middle latitudes, with no Earth in the sky and twilit nights; dark skies and radio quiet for astronomy, with towns lit by shielded, warm lamps.
far_side_places.third_dimension: Observatories on ridges, with high platforms near 70 km above for far-side astronomy.

high_latitude_towns.name: High-latitude towns
high_latitude_towns.character: Towns poleward of the latitude where a clear night never falls below the end of civil twilight, with the Sun's light wrapping round the Moon all night; dry, with the polar highs such as Nobile and Peary as bases for the polar sampling programme.
high_latitude_towns.third_dimension: Long, low light at every height; the regional magnets' cables would run through here.

undersea_communities.name: The undersea communities
undersea_communities.character: Enclosed domed communities on the submerged heritage sites, beginning with Tranquility Base under 467 m of water, reached by an access tower with a harbour and landing on the Sea of Tranquility.
undersea_communities.third_dimension: An access tower from the sea floor to a harbour at the surface.

answered: the dome's load by its shell and anchors

roaming_sky_towns.name: Roaming sky towns
roaming_sky_towns.character: Buoyant towns drifting with the winds about 10 km up, moving under power only to keep clear of storms and one another, to meet and to change course.
roaming_sky_towns.third_dimension: The whole town is aloft; sky boats and ferries run to the ground and between towns.

moored_or_streamlined_sky_towns.character: Buoyant towns that keep a place: moored by a tether over land or water, or streamlined hulls that hold a place, or follow the Sun to keep a time of day, under power.
moored_or_streamlined_sky_towns.third_dimension: Held at a chosen height over a chosen place, or over the moving terminator.

high_platforms.character: Long-endurance platforms near 70 km for far-side astronomy and nearside earthshine photometry, with research crews.

array_habitats.character: Spinning habitats on natural orbits beside the ring fleet. Workers commute in rotations, and the tinkerers who work at the array's industry most of the time live there.
array_habitats.third_dimension: Earth's gravity at 56 m radius at 4 rpm and the Moon's at 9.3 m, in one wheel.
